        <span class="guide-badge"><i class="fas fa-link"></i> Application Security</span>
        <h1>SBOM & Software Supply Chain Security: The Complete Guide</h1>
        <p style="color: var(--text-muted); font-size: 1.1rem;">CycloneDX vs SPDX deep dive, Syft/Trivy SBOM generation, SLSA framework levels, VEX vulnerability triage, CI/CD pipeline integration, and EO 14028/EU CRA compliance</p>
        <div style="margin-top: 1rem; color: var(--text-muted);">
            <span><i class="fas fa-book-open"></i> 30 min read</span> <span style="margin: 0 0.5rem;">|</span>
            <span><i class="fas fa-crosshairs"></i> Intermediate to Advanced</span> <span style="margin: 0 0.5rem;">|</span>
            <span><i class="far fa-calendar-alt"></i> February 2026</span>
        </div>
    </div>

    <img src="/images/guides/sbom-software-supply-chain-security.png" alt="SBOM Software Supply Chain Security Guide" class="featured-image" style="width: 100%; max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 12px; margin: 2rem 0; box-shadow: 0 10px 40px rgba(245,158,11,0.2); border: 1px solid var(--border);" loading="lazy">

    <div class="warning-box" style="margin-bottom: 2rem;">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-balance-scale"></i> Research Ethics:</strong>
        This document is published for defensive security research and educational purposes. Attack case studies are based on publicly disclosed incidents and post-mortems. Exploit code is presented solely for understanding defensive detection capabilities.
    </div>

    <div class="info-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-file-alt"></i> Abstract:</strong>
        The software supply chain is the #1 emerging attack surface in 2026. SolarWinds (2020), Log4Shell (2021), the XZ Utils backdoor (2024), and the Polyfill.io compromise (2024) proved that attackers are shifting from targeting applications directly to compromising their dependencies. A Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) is the foundational defense — a machine-readable inventory of every component in your software. This guide covers SBOM generation with Syft, Trivy, and cdxgen; deep comparison of CycloneDX vs SPDX formats; the SLSA framework for build integrity; VEX documents for vulnerability triage; CI/CD pipeline integration patterns; and compliance with US Executive Order 14028 and the EU Cyber Resilience Act.
    </div>

    <!-- SECTION 1: THREAT LANDSCAPE -->
    <h2 id="threat-landscape">1. Threat Landscape: Supply Chain Attacks in 2026</h2>

    <p>Software supply chain attacks have increased <strong>742%</strong> since 2019 (Sonatype State of Software Supply Chain 2025). The pattern is clear — attackers are targeting the weakest link:</p>

    <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Incident</th><th>Year</th><th>Vector</th><th>Impact</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr><td><strong>SolarWinds SUNBURST</strong></td><td>2020</td><td>Build system compromise — malicious code injected into Orion updates</td><td class="severity-critical">18,000 orgs, US government agencies</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Codecov Bash Uploader</strong></td><td>2021</td><td>CI/CD script modified to exfiltrate env vars</td><td class="severity-critical">29,000+ repos, credentials leaked</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Log4Shell (Log4j)</strong></td><td>2021</td><td>Zero-day in ubiquitous logging library</td><td class="severity-critical">Billions of devices, JNDI RCE</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>ua-parser-js NPM Hijack</strong></td><td>2021</td><td>Maintainer account compromise → cryptominer</td><td class="severity-high">8M weekly downloads compromised</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>PyTorch Torchtriton</strong></td><td>2022</td><td>Dependency confusion — malicious package on PyPI</td><td class="severity-high">Nightly builds compromised</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>3CX Supply Chain</strong></td><td>2023</td><td>Compromised via another supply chain attack (Trading Technologies)</td><td class="severity-critical">600,000 customers, Lazarus Group</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>XZ Utils Backdoor</strong></td><td>2024</td><td>Social engineering of maintainer → SSH backdoor</td><td class="severity-critical">Nearly all Linux distros, nation-state</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Polyfill.io</strong></td><td>2024</td><td>Domain acquisition → CDN serving malicious JS</td><td class="severity-critical">100,000+ websites, Chinese acquisition</td></tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

    <div class="architecture-diagram">
        <pre style="color: var(--accent-cyan); margin: 0;">
    SOFTWARE SUPPLY CHAIN ATTACK SURFACE
    ════════════════════════════════════

┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ │ SOURCE │───▶│ BUILD │───▶│ DEPLOY │───▶│ RUNTIME │ │ CODE │ │ SYSTEM │ │ PACKAGE │ │ │ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ │ │ │ │ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ │ATTACKS: │ │ATTACKS: │ │ATTACKS: │ │ATTACKS: │ │• Repo │ │• CI/CD │ │• Registry│ │• CDN │ │ hijack │ │ poison │ │ typosqat│ │ hijack │ │• Maintner│ │• Build │ │• Dep │ │• Dynamic │ │ takeover│ │ tamper │ │ confusn │ │ import │ │• Commit │ │• Compiler│ │• Package │ │• Runtime │ │ signing │ │ exploit │ │ swap │ │ inject │ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘

DEFENSE LAYERS: → SBOM: Know your ingredients at every stage → SLSA: Verify build integrity and provenance → VEX: Triage vulnerabilities in context → SCA: Continuous dependency scanning 

    <!-- SECTION 2: SBOM FUNDAMENTALS -->
    <h2 id="sbom-fundamentals">2. SBOM Fundamentals</h2>

    <h3>2.1 What Goes Into an SBOM</h3>
    <p>Per NTIA minimum elements (2021), every SBOM must contain:</p>
    <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Field</th><th>Description</th><th>Example</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr><td><strong>Supplier Name</strong></td><td>Entity that created the component</td><td>Apache Software Foundation</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Component Name</strong></td><td>Name of the package</td><td>log4j-core</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Version</strong></td><td>Exact version identifier</td><td>2.17.1</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Unique Identifier</strong></td><td>CPE, PURL, or SWID tag</td><td>pkg:maven/org.apache/log4j-core@2.17.1</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Dependency Relationship</strong></td><td>Direct or transitive</td><td>direct dependency of my-app</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Author</strong></td><td>SBOM creator</td><td>CI pipeline (build #4521)</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Timestamp</strong></td><td>When SBOM was generated</td><td>2026-02-18T15:30:00Z</td></tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

    <!-- SECTION 3: FORMATS -->
    <h2 id="formats">3. CycloneDX vs SPDX: Deep Comparison</h2>

    <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Feature</th><th>CycloneDX</th><th>SPDX</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr><td><strong>Maintainer</strong></td><td>OWASP</td><td>Linux Foundation (ISO 5962:2021)</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Primary Focus</strong></td><td>Security & vulnerability tracking</td><td>License compliance & IP</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Formats</strong></td><td>JSON, XML, Protobuf</td><td>JSON, YAML, XML, Tag-Value, RDF</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>VEX Support</strong></td><td>✅ Native (embedded)</td><td>⚠️ Via external SPDX-Security</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>BOM Types</strong></td><td>SBOM, SaaSBOM, HBOM, MBOM, OBOM</td><td>SBOM primarily</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>License Detail</strong></td><td>Basic (SPDX expression)</td><td>✅ Deep (concluded, declared, comments)</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Ecosystem</strong></td><td>Dependency-Track, Grype, OWASP tools</td><td>FOSSology, Augur, compliance tools</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Best For</strong></td><td>DevSecOps, vulnerability management</td><td>Legal compliance, license auditing</td></tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

    <div class="technical-box">
        <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> CycloneDX SBOM Example (JSON)</h3>
        <pre><code class="language-json">{

“bomFormat”: “CycloneDX”, “specVersion”: “1.6”, “serialNumber”: “urn:uuid:3e671687-395b-41f5-a30f-a58921a69b79”, “version”: 1, “metadata”: { “timestamp”: “2026-02-18T15:30:00Z”, “tools”: [{ “vendor”: “anchore”, “name”: “syft”, “version”: “1.18.0” }], “component”: { “type”: “application”, “name”: “my-api-service”, “version”: “3.2.1” } }, “components”: [ { “type”: “library”, “name”: “express”, “version”: “4.21.0”, “purl”: “pkg:npm/express@4.21.0”, “licenses”: [{ “license”: { “id”: “MIT” } }], “hashes”: [{ “alg”: “SHA-256”, “content”: “a1b2c3d4e5f6…” }], “externalReferences”: [{ “type”: “vcs”, “url”: “https://github.com/expressjs/express” }] }, { “type”: “library”, “name”: “lodash”, “version”: “4.17.21”, “purl”: “pkg:npm/lodash@4.17.21”, “licenses”: [{ “license”: { “id”: “MIT” } }] } ], “dependencies”: [ { “ref”: “my-api-service”, “dependsOn”: [“express”, “lodash”] } ] } 

    <!-- SECTION 4: GENERATION -->
    <h2 id="generation">4. SBOM Generation: Syft, Trivy, cdxgen</h2>

    <div class="technical-box">
        <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> Syft — Generate SBOM from Source/Image</h3>
        <pre><code class="language-bash"># Install Syft

curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh -s – -b /usr/local/bin

Generate CycloneDX SBOM from project directory

syft dir:./my-app -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.cdx.json

Generate SPDX SBOM from container image

syft registry:myorg/api:v3.2.1 -o spdx-json > sbom.spdx.json

Generate from Dockerfile (build-time analysis)

syft docker:myorg/api:latest -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.cdx.json

Include file metadata and secrets detection

syft dir:./my-app -o cyclonedx-json
–catalogers all
–source-name “my-api-service”
–source-version “3.2.1” > sbom.cdx.json 

    <div class="technical-box">
        <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> Trivy — SBOM + Vulnerability Scan in One</h3>
        <pre><code class="language-bash"># Install Trivy

curl -sfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aquasecurity/trivy/main/contrib/install.sh | sh -s – -b /usr/local/bin

Generate SBOM and scan for vulnerabilities simultaneously

trivy image –format cyclonedx –output sbom.cdx.json myorg/api:v3.2.1

Scan an existing SBOM for vulnerabilities

trivy sbom sbom.cdx.json

Generate SBOM from filesystem with license detection

trivy fs –format spdx-json –output sbom.spdx.json
–scanners vuln,license ./my-app

Scan and FAIL if critical vulns found (CI/CD gate)

trivy sbom sbom.cdx.json –exit-code 1 –severity CRITICAL,HIGH 

    <div class="technical-box">
        <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> cdxgen — Language-Aware CycloneDX Generator</h3>
        <pre><code class="language-bash"># Install cdxgen (supports 40+ languages)

npm install -g @cyclonedx/cdxgen

Generate SBOM (auto-detects language/framework)

cdxgen -o sbom.cdx.json ./my-app

Generate with vulnerability data embedded

cdxgen -o sbom.cdx.json –deep ./my-app

Generate for specific project type

cdxgen -t python -o sbom.cdx.json ./my-python-app cdxgen -t java -o sbom.cdx.json ./my-java-app 

    <!-- SECTION 5: SLSA -->
    <h2 id="slsa">5. SLSA Framework: Build Integrity Levels</h2>

    <p>SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts) answers the critical question: <strong>"Was this binary actually built from the source code I audited, by the build system I trust?"</strong></p>

    <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Level</th><th>Requirements</th><th>Protects Against</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr><td><strong>SLSA 1</strong></td><td>Build provenance exists (automated build, provenance document)</td><td>Accidental errors, basic tampering awareness</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>SLSA 2</strong></td><td>Signed provenance from a hosted build service (GitHub Actions, Cloud Build)</td><td>Tampering after build, unsigned artifacts</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>SLSA 3</strong></td><td>Hardened CI, non-falsifiable provenance, source-defined build</td><td>Compromised CI config, insider threats in pipeline</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>SLSA 4</strong></td><td>Hermetic/reproducible builds, full dependency provenance</td><td>Nation-state supply chain attacks (SolarWinds-class)</td></tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

    <div class="technical-box">
        <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> GitHub Actions — SLSA Level 3 Provenance</h3>
        <pre><code class="language-yaml"># .github/workflows/slsa-build.yml

name: SLSA Build with Provenance on: push: tags: [‘v*’]

permissions: id-token: write # For signing provenance contents: read attestations: write

jobs: build: runs-on: ubuntu-latest outputs: digest: ${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }} steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4

  - name: Build artifact
    id: build
    run: |
      npm ci --ignore-scripts  # Deterministic install
      npm run build
      DIGEST=$(sha256sum dist/app.tar.gz | cut -d' ' -f1)
      echo "digest=sha256:${DIGEST}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  - name: Generate SBOM
    run: |
      syft dir:. -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.cdx.json

  # SLSA Provenance — creates signed, non-falsifiable build attestation
  - name: Attest Build Provenance
    uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@v2
    with:
      subject-name: 'myorg/api'
      subject-digest: ${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}
      push-to-registry: true

  # SBOM Attestation — links SBOM to the artifact
  - name: Attest SBOM
    uses: actions/attest-sbom@v1
    with:
      subject-name: 'myorg/api'
      subject-digest: ${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}
      sbom-path: 'sbom.cdx.json'</code></pre>
    </div>

    <!-- SECTION 6: VEX -->
    <h2 id="vex">6. VEX: Vulnerability Exploitability Exchange</h2>

    <p>An SBOM tells you <em>what</em> components you have. A VEX document tells you <em>whether the vulnerability in that component actually affects your product</em>. This solves the "alert fatigue" problem — not every CVE in a dependency is exploitable in your context.</p>

    <table>
        <thead><tr><th>VEX Status</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Example</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr><td><strong>Not Affected</strong></td><td>Vulnerability exists in component but is not exploitable in this product</td><td>Log4Shell in log4j used only for compile-time annotation processing</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Affected</strong></td><td>Vulnerability is exploitable — action required</td><td>Spring4Shell in a web app with ClassPathBeanDefinitionScanner exposed</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Fixed</strong></td><td>Was affected, now patched</td><td>Updated lodash from 4.17.20 to 4.17.21</td></tr>
            <tr><td><strong>Under Investigation</strong></td><td>Still determining exploitability</td><td>New CVE disclosed, analysis in progress</td></tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

    <div class="technical-box">
        <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> CycloneDX VEX Document</h3>

“bomFormat”: “CycloneDX”, “specVersion”: “1.6”, “vulnerabilities”: [ { “id”: “CVE-2024-50623”, “source”: { “name”: “NVD” }, “ratings”: [ { “severity”: “critical”, “score”: 9.8, “method”: “CVSSv31” } ], “analysis”: { “state”: “not_affected”, “justification”: “code_not_reachable”, “detail”: “The vulnerable file upload endpoint (CleoConnectClient) is not exposed in our deployment — we use only the SFTP module which does not process the affected parameter.”, “response”: [“workaround_available”] }, “affects”: [{ “ref”: “pkg:maven/com.cleo/vlnavigator@5.7.0.0” }] } ] } 

    <!-- SECTION 7: CICD -->
    <h2 id="cicd">7. CI/CD Pipeline Integration</h2>

    <div class="architecture-diagram">
        <pre style="color: var(--accent-cyan); margin: 0;">
            SBOM-INTEGRATED CI/CD PIPELINE
            ═════════════════════════════

┌──────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ │ CODE │───▶│ BUILD │───▶│ SCAN │───▶│ DEPLOY │ │ PUSH │ │ │ │ │ │ │ └──────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ │ │ │ ┌───▼────┐ ┌───▼────┐ ┌───▼────┐ │Generate│ │ Trivy │ │ Attest │ │ SBOM │ │ Scan │ │ SLSA │ │(Syft) │ │ SBOM │ │Provnce │ └───┬────┘ └───┬────┘ └───┬────┘ │ │ │ ┌───▼────┐ ┌───▼────┐ ┌───▼────┐ │ Upload │ │ GATE: │ │ Store │ │ to Dep │ │ Block │ │ in OCI │ │ Track │ │ if P0 │ │Registry│ └────────┘ └────────┘ └────────┘ 

    <div class="technical-box">
        <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> Complete CI Pipeline with SBOM Gate</h3>
        <pre><code class="language-yaml"># .github/workflows/sbom-pipeline.yml

name: SBOM Security Pipeline on: [push, pull_request]

jobs: sbom-scan: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4

  - name: Build Application
    run: npm ci && npm run build

  # Step 1: Generate SBOM
  - name: Generate SBOM (CycloneDX)
    run: |
      curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anchore/syft/main/install.sh | sh -s
      syft dir:. -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.cdx.json
      echo "Components found: $(jq '.components | length' sbom.cdx.json)"

  # Step 2: Vulnerability scan with gate
  - name: Scan SBOM for Vulnerabilities
    run: |
      curl -sfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aquasecurity/trivy/main/contrib/install.sh | sh -s
      trivy sbom sbom.cdx.json \
        --exit-code 1 \
        --severity CRITICAL \
        --format json \
        --output vuln-report.json
    continue-on-error: false  # FAIL the build on CRITICAL

  # Step 3: License compliance check
  - name: Check Licenses
    run: |
      # Extract all licenses from SBOM
      jq -r '.components[].licenses[]?.license.id // "UNKNOWN"' \
        sbom.cdx.json | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
      
      # Fail on copyleft licenses in proprietary project
      BANNED=$(jq -r '.components[] | select(.licenses[]?.license.id == "GPL-3.0-only") | .name' sbom.cdx.json)
      if [ -n "$BANNED" ]; then
        echo "❌ GPL-3.0 components found: $BANNED"
        exit 1
      fi

  # Step 4: Upload to Dependency-Track
  - name: Upload SBOM to Dependency-Track
    run: |
      curl -X POST "https://dtrack.internal.company.com/api/v1/bom" \
        -H "X-Api-Key: ${{ secrets.DTRACK_API_KEY }}" \
        -H "Content-Type: multipart/form-data" \
        -F "autoCreate=true" \
        -F "projectName=my-api-service" \
        -F "projectVersion=${{ github.sha }}" \
        -F "bom=@sbom.cdx.json"

  # Step 5: Store SBOM as build artifact
  - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
    with:
      name: sbom
      path: sbom.cdx.json</code></pre>
    </div>

    <!-- SECTION 8: ATTACK CASE STUDIES -->
    <h2 id="attack-defense">8. Attack Case Studies & Detection</h2>

    <h3>8.1 XZ Utils Backdoor (CVE-2024-3094) — The Social Engineering Supply Chain Attack</h3>
    <div class="attack-scenario">
        <p><strong>The Attack:</strong> Over 2+ years, a pseudonymous contributor ("Jia Tan") systematically gained trust of the sole XZ Utils maintainer through helpful contributions. After becoming a co-maintainer, they injected an obfuscated backdoor into the build system (not the source code) that would execute during compilation on Debian/RPM-based systems. The backdoor hijacked the SSH authentication flow via systemd's dependency on liblzma, allowing the attacker to execute arbitrary commands before authentication.</p>
        <p><strong>Why SBOMs Help:</strong> An SBOM tracking build-time dependencies and provenance would have flagged that the liblzma binary did not match a clean build from the audited source code — a SLSA Level 3 violation.</p>
        <p><strong>Detection:</strong> Compare binary hash in SBOM against reproducible build output. Mismatch = compromised build pipeline.</p>
    </div>

    <h3>8.2 Detection: YARA Rule for Malicious NPM Packages</h3>
    <div class="technical-box">
        <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> YARA Rule: Suspicious NPM Install Scripts</h3>
        <pre><code class="language-yaml">rule npm_supply_chain_indicators {
meta:
    description = "Detects suspicious patterns in NPM packages"
    author = "TheHGTech"
    date = "2026-02-18"
    severity = "high"

strings:
    // Obfuscated eval patterns
    $eval1 = /eval\s*\(\s*Buffer\.from\s*\(/ nocase
    $eval2 = /eval\s*\(\s*atob\s*\(/ nocase
    
    // DNS/HTTP exfiltration in install scripts
    $exfil1 = /https?:\/\/[a-z0-9]{8,}\./ nocase
    $exfil2 = /child_process.*exec.*curl/ nocase
    $exfil3 = /child_process.*exec.*wget/ nocase
    
    // Environment variable harvesting
    $env1 = /process\.env\.(AWS_|GITHUB_TOKEN|NPM_TOKEN)/ nocase
    $env2 = /os\.environ\[.(AWS_|GITHUB|CI_)/ nocase
    
    // Suspicious install script targets
    $install1 = "preinstall" 
    $install2 = "postinstall"

condition:
    any of ($eval*) or
    (any of ($exfil*) and any of ($install*)) or
    (any of ($env*) and any of ($exfil*))

}

    <!-- SECTION 10: AUDIT -->
    <h2 id="audit">10. Audit & Continuous Monitoring</h2>

    <div class="success-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-clipboard-check"></i> SBOM Maturity Audit Checklist:</strong>
        <pre><code class="language-bash">#!/bin/bash

sbom-maturity-audit.sh — Assess your SBOM program maturity

echo “=== SBOM Maturity Assessment ===”

Level 1: Basic

echo “[L1] SBOM Exists?” if [ -f “sbom.cdx.json” ] || [ -f “sbom.spdx.json” ]; then echo “ ✅ SBOM file found“ COMPONENTS=$(jq ‘.components | length’ sbom.cdx.json 2>/dev/null || echo “0”) echo “ 📦 Components inventoried: $COMPONENTS“ else echo “ ❌ No SBOM found — Level 0“ exit 1 fi

Level 2: Format Compliance

echo “[L2] Format Compliance?” FORMAT=$(jq -r ‘.bomFormat // “unknown”’ sbom.cdx.json 2>/dev/null) VERSION=$(jq -r ‘.specVersion // “unknown”’ sbom.cdx.json 2>/dev/null) echo “ Format: $FORMAT $VERSION“

Level 3: Vulnerability Scanning

echo “[L3] Vulnerability Integration?” if command -v trivy &> /dev/null; then VULNS=$(trivy sbom sbom.cdx.json –format json 2>/dev/null | jq ‘.Results[]?.Vulnerabilities | length’ | paste -sd+ | bc) echo “ 🔍 Known vulnerabilities: ${VULNS:-0}“ else echo “ ⚠️ No vulnerability scanner configured“ fi

Level 4: SLSA Provenance

echo “[L4] Build Provenance?” if [ -f “provenance.intoto.jsonl” ]; then echo “ ✅ SLSA provenance attestation found“ else echo “ ⚠️ No SLSA provenance — build integrity unverified“ fi

Level 5: Continuous Monitoring

echo “[L5] Dependency-Track Integration?” DTRACK_URL=“${DTRACK_URL:-https://dtrack.internal.company.com}” STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w “%{http_code}” “$DTRACK_URL/api/version” 2>/dev/null) if [ “$STATUS” = “200” ]; then echo “ ✅ Dependency-Track reachable“ else echo “ ⚠️ Dependency-Track not configured“ fi

echo “” echo “=== Assessment Complete ===”
